It is open to school students aged 15+, university students and anyone interested in tech, marketing and content creation. Only the first 90 registered participants can attend.

summary.en: A case competition in which university teams analyse a real dilemma faced by the National Bank of Georgia and present policy recommendations to central bankers. Prizes are 4,000, 2,000 and 1,500 GEL for the top three teams.

summary.ar: مسابقة حالات دراسية تحلل فيها فرق جامعية معضلة حقيقية يواجهها البنك الوطني الجورجي وتقدّم توصيات إلى لجنة من مسؤولي البنك. الجوائز 4,000 و2,000 و1,500 لاري للفرق الثلاثة الأولى.

about.en:
"Regulator's Dilemma" is the National Bank of Georgia's annual student competition, run through its FINEDU financial-education platform with support from Credo Bank. Teams receive a real dilemma from central-bank work, analyse it and present practical recommendations to a jury of at least three NBG experts.

Teams of 3-6 bachelor or master students from the same authorised Georgian university register online; only the first 20 teams get into round one. Five teams reach the final round and three winners share prizes of 4,000, 2,000 and 1,500 GEL (split among members). In 2026 registration was 19-25 October, round one 16-17 November and the final on 7 December.

It is an excellent way for economics, finance and law students to understand monetary policy and supervision and to get noticed by the central bank.

en: Work on a real central-bank policy dilemma
Present to NBG experts; prizes up to 4,000 GEL
Strong CV signal for economics/finance careers

eligibility.en: Teams of 3-6 students enrolled in bachelor or master programmes at the same authorised higher education institution in Georgia (members may be from different years and faculties). Working language Georgian.

en: Watch finedu.gov.ge events in early October 2027 for the call
Form a team of 3-6 students from your university
Register via the online form as soon as registration opens (first 20 teams only)
Solve the first-round assignment and email it to info@finedu.gov.ge
Present to the jury; finalists get a second assignment

score_reason: Prestigious annual case competition; 2027 dates estimated

summary.ar: مسابقة رسم للأطفال من 6 إلى 17 عامًا ينظمها البنك الوطني الجورجي كل مارس ضمن أسبوع المال العالمي. في 2026 صمّم المشاركون ورقة نقدية لمنطقتهم، وحصل سبعة فائزين على 500 لاري لكل منهم.

about.en:
Every March, the National Bank of Georgia's FINEDU platform celebrates Global Money Week with creative competitions for children. In 2026 the theme was "My Region - My Banknote": entrants hand-drew both sides of a banknote representing their city, village or region, including security features such as a serial number and security thread.

It is open to children and teens aged 6-17 in three age groups (6-9, 10-13, 14-17). Entries are posted as a comment on FINEDU's official Facebook competition post (parents submit for under-16s). A jury from the NBG and partner banks picks two winners per age group, plus a public-vote winner; each received 500 GEL plus educational gifts.

The theme changes each year, so check finedu.gov.ge in March 2027.

en: Cash prizes (500 GEL per winner in 2026)
Three age groups from 6 to 17
Fun way to learn about money and banknotes

eligibility.en: Children and teenagers aged 6-17 (2026 rules). Prizes are paid into a bank account in Georgia. Entries in Georgian context.

en: Check finedu.gov.ge events in March 2027 for the theme and rules
Create a hand-made artwork (no digital or AI images)
Post a clear photo as a comment on the official FINEDU Facebook competition post with name and age (parent submits for under-16s)

costs.en: Free. Prizes paid by the National Bank of Georgia and partner banks.

score_reason: Easy, free, annual national competition for younger students

summary.en: Adjara residents aged 18-35 can win a funded professional internship in a European region through the Eurodyssey exchange of the Assembly of European Regions. Host regions pay a monthly stipend of 700-1,200 EUR plus a language course, and Adjara adds 2,000 GEL.
summary.ka: აჭარაში რეგისტრირებულ 18-35 წლის ახალგაზრდებს შეუძლიათ ევროპის რეგიონთა ასამბლეის „ევროოდისეას“ პროგრამით ევროპულ რეგიონში დაფინანსებული სტაჟირება მოიპოვონ. მასპინძელი რეგიონი იხდის ყოველთვიურ სტიპენდიას 700-1200 ევროს ოდენობით და ენის კურსს, ხოლო აჭარის სამინისტრო დამატებით 2000 ლარს გასცემს.
summary.ar: يمكن للشباب المسجلين في أجارا (18-35 عامًا) الحصول على تدريب مهني ممول في إقليم أوروبي عبر برنامج يوروديسي التابع لجمعية الأقاليم الأوروبية. يدفع الإقليم المضيف منحة شهرية من 700 إلى 1,200 يورو ودورة لغة، وتضيف وزارة أجارا 2,000 لاري.

about.en:
Since 2006 the Adjara Ministry of Education and Sport has run Georgia's entry into Eurodyssey, the youth exchange programme of the Assembly of European Regions (founded 1985). Participants complete a professional internship in a member region in Europe to build work skills and language ability.

Internships last several months depending on the host region and are fully funded by the host: a monthly stipend of 700-1,200 EUR covers food and accommodation, and the internship starts with an intensive language course and a cultural programme. AER co-funds insurance; the intern pays travel and visa costs, and after completion the Adjara ministry pays a one-off 2,000 GEL.

Selection has two stages: the ministry's own competition, then registration on eurodyssey.aer.eu and a remote interview with the host region and employer, who make the final decision.

en: Monthly stipend of 700-1,200 EUR paid by the host region
Free intensive language course in the host country
Extra 2,000 GEL from the Adjara ministry after completion

eligibility.en: Citizens of Georgia aged 18-35 registered in the Autonomous Republic of Adjara, with a vocational or higher education diploma and knowledge of a foreign language, who meet the host region's requirements.

en: Read the regulation and document list on the ministry's "Internship abroad" page
Submit the application form and documents to the ministry during the announced registration period
Pass the ministry's first-stage selection
Register your profile on eurodyssey.aer.eu
Interview remotely with the host region and employer

costs.en: Host region pays a 700-1,200 EUR monthly stipend and language course; travel and visa paid by the intern; 2,000 GEL one-off support from Adjara after completion.

about.en:
The Environmental Information and Education Centre (EIEC), a public body under Georgia's Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture, offers a free online course on environmental democracy - the first of its kind in Georgian.

The course has two modules and aims to strengthen knowledge of environmental rights and responsibilities and of how the public can participate in environmental decision-making (access to information, consultations, appeals). It suits school students, university students, activists and anyone interested in environmental policy.

Registration is online at any time via the EIEC course page.

en: Free, online and self-paced
Learn how to use environmental rights in practice
Good grounding for law, policy and environmental studies

eligibility.en: Anyone who reads Georgian; no prerequisites.

en: Open the course page on eiec.gov.ge
Click the registration link and create your account
Complete the two modules at your own pace

score_reason: Free, always open, but Georgian-only and short

about.en:
The EIEC, Georgia's state centre for environmental education, offers free webinars throughout the year for school students, teachers and other interested groups on environmental and agricultural topics such as climate change, biodiversity, waste, water and sustainable farming.

A school, club or youth group chooses a topic and the centre plans the webinar for the right age group. It is an easy way for an eco-club or class to bring in an expert speaker.

about.en:
The Young Volunteers Network of Georgia's Environmental Information and Education Centre brings together young people aged 15-17 and supports their active involvement in educational activities at local level.

Volunteers gain knowledge and experience, develop skills and make friends while contributing to sustainable development. Topics include communication and presentation skills, the Sustainable Development Goals, climate change and its risks, biodiversity, forest and water management, renewable energy, waste management and ecosystem services.

Members are selected through an annual call; the 2026 cohort is active, so watch the EIEC youth programmes page for the next intake.

Lead real activities in your community
Volunteering record for university applications

Join the training and start local activities

about.en:
Green Camp "Climate Ambassadors" is run by Georgia's Environmental Information and Education Centre to raise young people's awareness of environmental issues and prepare them to implement projects locally after the camp.

The programme covers forest management, biodiversity, atmospheric air quality, climate change and disaster risk reduction, community-based disaster risk management, Georgia's geological hazards and the role of the National Environmental Agency's hydrometeorology department. Participants work with specialists on topics that interest them and take part in team activities.

The camp runs annually; watch the EIEC youth programmes page for the next call.

en: Learn from Georgia's environmental specialists
Team activities and hands-on topics
Become a local Climate Ambassador

Apply with the published form
If selected, attend the camp and then run a local project

about.en:
Every year Georgia's Ministry of Education, Science and Youth, through the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation, selects, trains and sends national teams to the priority international school olympiads, including the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO).

Candidates are the strongest finishers of the National School Olympiad (run by the National Assessment and Examinations Center), chosen under the olympiad rules. They sit two selection rounds organised by the Foundation; the best become team members (plus reserves) and are trained by a team of Foundation coaches (leader, deputy leader and assistants). The Foundation administers and funds the delegation's participation abroad.

In 2026 the rules were issued on 13 March and the IMO rounds took place in April. To be considered for 2027, compete in the 2026-27 National School Olympiad in mathematics.

en: Route to represent Georgia at the IMO
Free coaching by the Foundation's team of trainers
Travel and participation fully funded

eligibility.en: School students in Georgia selected as candidates on the basis of National School Olympiad results in mathematics (and any age limits set by the IMO rules).

en: Register for and compete in the 2026-27 National School Olympiad in mathematics
Reach the top finishers so you are invited as a team candidate
Submit the candidate application form when the Foundation publishes the 2027 rules (around March)
Sit the two selection rounds in spring 2027
If selected, train with the national team coaches

costs.en: Free. Training, travel and participation at the international olympiad are funded by the state through the Foundation.

score_reason: Top-tier pathway to an international olympiad, fully funded

about.en:
Every year Georgia's Ministry of Education, Science and Youth, through the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation, selects, trains and sends national teams to the priority international school olympiads, including the International Biology Olympiad (IBO).

Candidates are the strongest finishers of the National School Olympiad (run by the National Assessment and Examinations Center), chosen under the olympiad rules. They sit two selection rounds organised by the Foundation; the best become team members (plus reserves) and are trained by a team of Foundation coaches (leader, deputy leader and assistants). The Foundation administers and funds the delegation's participation abroad.

In 2026 the rules were issued on 13 March and the IBO rounds took place in April. To be considered for 2027, compete in the 2026-27 National School Olympiad in biology.

en: Route to represent Georgia at the IBO
Free coaching by the Foundation's team of trainers
Travel and participation fully funded

eligibility.en: School students in Georgia selected as candidates on the basis of National School Olympiad results in biology (and any age limits set by the IBO rules).

en: Register for and compete in the 2026-27 National School Olympiad in biology
Reach the top finishers so you are invited as a team candidate
Submit the candidate application form when the Foundation publishes the 2027 rules (around March)
Sit the two selection rounds in spring 2027
If selected, train with the national team coaches

costs.en: Free. Training, travel and participation at the international olympiad are funded by the state through the Foundation.

score_reason: Top-tier pathway to an international olympiad, fully funded

Missions include embassies across Europe, the Gulf (Qatar, Kuwait, UAE), the USA, Canada and China and the UN missions in Geneva and New York.

about.en:
As part of the state paid internship programme initiated by Georgia's Prime Minister, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is recruiting interns for three-month paid placements at Georgian diplomatic missions abroad, starting in 2027.

It is open to citizens of Georgia who are studying in, or have graduated from, an accredited bachelor's, master's or doctoral programme (higher or vocational education) abroad. Host missions include the embassies in Belgium, Spain, Germany, France, Italy, Greece, the Czech Republic, the UK, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, the Netherlands, Egypt, Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE, Jordan, the USA, Canada, the Holy See and China, plus the Permanent Missions to the UN in Geneva and New York. Pay is set under Georgian legislation.

Each mission publishes its own announcement (linked from the MFA notice); documents are sent to that mission's official email by 8 November 2026. It is a rare chance to gain diplomatic work experience in the city where you already study.

en: Paid diplomatic work experience at an embassy or UN mission
Placements in 20+ countries including Qatar, UAE and Kuwait
Part of a national state internship programme

eligibility.en: Citizens of Georgia studying at, or graduated from, an accredited bachelor's, master's or doctoral (or vocational) programme abroad. Other requirements are set by each mission's announcement.

en: Open the MFA announcement and the linked notice of the mission in your country
Prepare the documents listed by that mission (CV, proof of study/graduation, etc.)
Email them to the mission's official address by 8 November 2026
Attend any interview the mission arranges

costs.en: Paid internship; the amount is set under Georgian legislation. No application fee.

score_reason: Paid embassy internships worldwide, closing 8 Nov

about.en:
Georgia's central bank runs an internship (practice) track for students alongside its vacancies. On the career section of nbg.gov.ge, applicants select the category or department where they would like to intern (for example monetary policy, financial stability, supervision, statistics, legal, IT) and upload their academic transcript and CV.

There is no fixed call window: applications are kept and matched to department needs. It suits economics, finance, law, statistics and computer science students who want real experience at the country's main economic institution.

en: Experience inside Georgia's central bank
Choose the department you want
Apply any time online

eligibility.en: University students (and recent graduates) able to work in Georgian; specific requirements depend on the department.

en: Open the internships page on nbg.gov.ge
Select the area where you want to intern
Upload your transcript and CV and submit
Wait to be contacted if a department has a place

costs.en: No application fee; compensation is not stated on the page.

about.en:
Since 2016 Georgia has held a Science and Innovation Festival every autumn, coordinated by the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation with the Ministry of Education. Universities, research centres, the National Academy of Sciences, museums, libraries and publishers across Georgia run public events.

Formats include conferences, public lectures, workshops, science-popular experiments, exhibitions, science cafes and shows, competitions, quizzes and special events for school students. Venues include university campuses, the Georgian National Museum and libraries in Tbilisi and the regions.

For students it is the easiest way to visit labs, meet researchers and try experiments for free; universities and schools can also propose events that showcase student research.

en: Free labs, lectures and science shows across Georgia
Special events for school students
Meet researchers and visit universities

eligibility.en: Open to the public; most events are free and walk-in. Institutions (universities, research centres, schools) can propose events.

en: Check the festival page and Facebook from September 2027 for the programme
Pick events in your city (some need online registration)
Attend; teachers can book class visits where offered
